research_method.claude: Online quantitative survey; Mini-IPIP (20 items), Collective Self-Esteem scale (16 items), 3-item perceived team productivity (5-point Likert); multiple linear regression with nine predictors and backward elimination (alpha = .10); VIF, Durbin-Watson, residual and Q-Q checks
research_method.nlm: Online survey; Mini-IPIP (20 items), Luhtanen and Crocker CSE scale (16 items), 3 self-assessed productivity items (5-point Likert); multiple linear regression with backward elimination; VIF and Durbin-Watson diagnostics
research_method.value: Cross-sectional online survey (short communication); Big Five via Mini-IPIP (20 items), Collective Self-Esteem scale (16 items) and 3-item self-assessed team productivity, all 5-point Likert; multiple linear regression with nine predictors and backward elimination (alpha = .10); assumption checks (VIF, Durbin-Watson, residual and Q-Q plots); n = 71

cat_productivity.note: Borderline: perceived team productivity is the dependent variable, but it is the mean of three self-assessed Likert items (perceived productivity, which the definition routes to cat_survey). Author to confirm.

cat_quality.note: Borderline: 'delivers software with high quality' is one self-report item inside the productivity composite (Claude tags the composite Productivity/Delivery/Quality); no quality metric.

cat_collaboration.note: Both tag Collective Self-Esteem (team social identity: membership esteem, public/private CSE) as Collaboration/Social identity; borderline fit (group identification rather than communication or coordination).

cat_delivery.note: Borderline: 'delivers software on time' is one self-report item inside the productivity composite.

cat_survey.note: All constructs self-reported on Likert scales.

evidence.quote: Personality was measured using the Mini-IPIP [11], a 20-item scale (four items per Big Five trait) rated on a 5-point Likert scale. Social identity was measured using the Collective Self-Esteem scale [10], with 16 items (four per CSE dimension) rated on a 5-point Likert scale.

Team productivity was operationalized as the mean of three self-assessed items: "The team delivers software on time", "The team delivers software with high quality", and "We are an effective team" (5-point Likert scale).
We used multiple linear regression with backward elimination.

We distributed an online survey through five open-source software (OSS) project developer mailing lists: Apache OpenOffice, Mozilla (web, general, and extension development), Eclipse, Python-dev, and VirtualBox.
We received 71 complete responses: software developers (50.7%), project managers (22.6%), team/tech leads (14.0%), and UX/UI designers (12.7%).
Social identity was measured using the Collective Self-Esteem scale [10], with 16 items (four per CSE dimension) rated on a 5-point Likert scale.
